answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller, whether trading opal, sourcing velvet, or booking summit venues, to lock a fixed bond before accepting work. The bond stays locked through a dispute window and is slashed when signed transaction records prove non-delivery. Creating more identities does not create more collateral: an attacker running 1,000 sellers must fund 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and risking its loss on fraudulent trades.
